topic: How can frequency planning address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems?
consensus_response: Frequency planning can mitigate interference by allocating non-overlapping bands, implementing exclusion zones, and using adaptive techniques like cognitive radio. Beamforming with phased array antennas spatially separates signals, reducing spectral overlap. Adaptive modulation schemes optimize coexistence, minimizing interference and enhancing system capacity.
reference_context: Satellite communication systems operate on specific frequency bands, such as S, L, Ku, and Ka bands, which may overlap with broadband power line communications, requiring careful frequency planning to minimize interference.
